assertions.name: C1
assertions.source: C1: the k-strand Markov measure sums to 1 for k = 1..20 - S is the entropy of a genuine state, not of an unnormalised weight

assertions.name: C2
assertions.source: C2: reproduces Addendum 23's balanced-cut table (E0*S(floor(1.5A)) at A = 2, 4, 6, 12) to the four decimals it publishes - same object, so the verdict below is about theirs

assertions.name: A1
assertions.source: A1: S(3A) > 0 at EVERY A - Addendum 23's "at w = 3 the cut is the entire system and the entropy is identically zero" is FALSE. S is a TRACE-state entropy: S(6) = 2.84368687, S(12) = 6.664991078

assertions.name: A2
assertions.source: A2: S is NOT symmetric under k <-> n-k (S(1) = 0 vs S(5) = 2.2124 at n = 6) - so it is not a pure-state bipartition entropy, no Schmidt argument applies, and there is no "balanced cut is the maximiser" justification available for w = 3/2 either

assertions.name: A3
assertions.source: A3: S(k)/k is STRICTLY INCREASING over k = 1..64 - the entropy density rises with the cut width

assertions.name: A4
assertions.source: A4: and it approaches ln[2]_q = 0.6985808249 strictly from BELOW, and SLOWLY - at k = 64 the density is still 6.57242 % short (S(64)/64 = 0.6526671341). So the asymptotic `E0*w*ln[2]_q per nucleon` OVERSTATES the model in the light-nucleus range, where k is single- or double-digit

assertions.name: A5
assertions.source: A5: g_w(4) <= g_w(6) for ALL 581 values of w on a 0.005 grid over [0.10, 3.00] - the model's per-nucleon prediction never decreases from 4He to 6Li. (A grid used to FALSIFY a universal claim, not to select a w)

assertions.name: A6
assertions.source: A6: but the DATA decreases there - B/A is 7.0739156 at 4He and 5.3323312 at 6Li. This is the 4He peak, a fact about AME, not about this framework

assertions.name: A7
assertions.source: A7: THE EXCLUSION - for every w and every positive overall scale c, c*g_w(4) <= c*g_w(6) while B/A decreases across those two isotopes, so no member of the family matches both. The failure is in the SHAPE, not the normalisation

description: Excludes the one-parameter growing-width cut of Addendum 23 Front 1 WITHOUT selecting any w. S(k)/k is increasing, so the model's per-nucleon prediction is non-decreasing in A for every fixed w; the AME per-nucleon binding is not, peaking at 4He (7.0739) and dipping at 6Li (5.3323). A non-decreasing function cannot match a function that decreases across the same two points, and an arbitrary positive rescaling preserves that -- so the failure is in the SHAPE, not the normalisation, and the family is excluded scope (b). Also corrects Addendum 23's claim that the entropy is identically zero at w = 3: S(3A) > 0 at every A, because S is a TRACE-state entropy, not a pure-state bipartition entropy (it is not even symmetric under k <-> n-k).

data.verdict: scope-(b): the one-parameter constant-w growing-width cut, and any overall rescaling of it, is excluded by the monotonicity of S(k)/k against the non-monotonicity of B/A. A cut whose width depends on the isotope's own structure is NOT excluded.
data.corrects: Addendum 23 Front 1: 'at w = 3 the cut is the entire system and the entropy is identically zero' is false; S(3A) > 0 at every A.

caveats: Scope (b) and narrow: what is excluded is the one-parameter family 'cut of width wA with w constant across isotopes', together with any overall positive rescaling of it. A cut whose width depends on the isotope's own structure is NOT excluded, and nothing here says what the missing binding term is.

No w is selected anywhere. The grid over w scans to FALSIFY a universal monotonicity claim, which is the legitimate direction; it never picks a best-scoring w. The sqrt(rmax/rmin) figure is a closed-form identity verified, not a fitted optimum.
S(k)/k is measured monotone over k = 1..64, not proved monotone for all k. The exclusion needs it only on the range the isotopes reach.
